designSummary: Cost-effectiveness analysis alongside a comparison of tutorial groups allocated by timetable block; clustering by tutorial group.
sampleSize: One class of about 180 students gives about 90 per arm. With pass rates near 87 percent, a 95 percent interval for the difference in pass proportions is about 10 percentage points either side of the estimate before allowing for clustering, so one year cannot show non-inferiority within a 5-point margin; that would need about 700 students per arm. The analysis therefore reports the probability that the near-peer option is cost-effective at stated values per additional student passing, and plans to add the 2028 class before any firm conclusion.
primaryAnalysis: Difference in first-attempt pass proportion between arms from a mixed-effects logistic model with tutorial group as a random effect and first-year assessment score as a covariate; incremental cost per student; non-parametric bootstrap of 5,000 resamples by tutorial group for the joint distribution of cost and effect; cost-effectiveness acceptability curve.
secondaryAnalysis: Sensitivity analyses valuing tutor time at the research assistant rate and at zero, and excluding calibration costs; faculty hours released.
missingData: Students who do not sit the May OSCE are reported by arm; the primary analysis includes students who sat it, with a sensitivity analysis counting absentees as not passing.
multiplicity: One primary effect measure; other analyses are labelled as secondary or sensitivity.
software: R (lme4 and boot packages); code written before the OSCE results are released.
overfittingGuards: One adjustment variable fixed in advance
Values per additional student passing stated before results
summary: About 90 students per arm; results as probabilities of cost-effectiveness, with a second year planned before firm conclusions.
